_note: A finished run needs three answers from the dashboard's AI endpoint, so the
probe mounts `AgentPlan` at `phase: "done"` with three applied steps — a
state the runner really produces (`advance()` past the last step sets
"done" and leaves each approved step marked `applied`).
WHAT THE BOARD DRAWS THAT THE CODE DOES NOT, and why the code wins:
171:91 `Actions` (a Stop under a finished run), 171:94 the success-tint
`Diff` block, and 171:99/171:101 `Discard` / `Apply`. That pair is the
census note `drift-applied-not-proposed-no-discard`, and it was ruled on
before this pass: LEDGER J-171:67, wave F, 2026-09-04 — 'each approved step
applies in its own transaction, so at "done" there is nothing left to
discard. The board's batch Discard+Apply is deliberately not built.' The
agent path proposes per step (board 170:97, built) and offers Undo all; a
batch Apply at the end would have to hold three edits unapplied, which is a
different runner. Nothing here re-opens that.
171:103/171:104 `note` is a designer annotation, not UI — the 2026-09-03
founder ruling on note blocks (LEDGER J-164:22) covers this one by name.
step-1-title carries no spec: 171:82 fixes the label at 208 wide, which is
the board's 280 frame less its 56 left offset and 16 right gutter. Its type
(12/18, ink) does match; the width is the same 280-vs-299 board/inspector
conflict `ai-idle` records in full. Its glyph and index ARE compared, and
the row's own 40 height is compared three times over.
